input.question: What is the evolutionary purpose of having different blood types (A,B,AB,O)?
input.ground_truth: While this doesn't answer your question, it is important to understand that evolution does not have a purpose. Mutations do not happen because they can be beneficial. Random mutations happen in individuals, then over time if the mutation is beneficial and propagated via offspring, the lineage with that trait may be more fit than individuals without that trait and slowly become more predominant. A more accurate question would be "Why did organisms evolve different blood types?" I'm not trying to be pedantic for the sake of pedantry, but I think maybe this will help you understand other's answers a little more clearly.

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your blood is like a team of special helpers that travel around your body to keep you healthy. The different blood types—A, B, AB, and O—are like different kinds of uniforms that these helpers can wear.

Long, long ago, people’s bodies started to make these different uniforms because it helped them fight off sickness in different ways. For example, if a germ tried to make someone sick, having a different "uniform" might help the body spot the germ and fight it better.

So, having different blood types is like having different superhero costumes. Some costumes are better at fighting certain germs. Over a long, long time, people with different costumes (blood types) survived better and had more babies. That’s why we have many blood types today!

Also, if someone needs a blood transfusion (when they need someone else’s blood), having different blood types helps people get the right kind of help when they need it. But mostly, it’s because it helped people’s bodies stay strong and healthy against different sicknesses over many, many years.
